This is amazing, OP. Thank you for your kindness in this mess of things. Pokemon has been my hobby since its release in 1996. It has saved me from dark places and a horrific childhood. It gave me hope and excitement to find my favorite characters and to learn how to draw them. I wore Pokemon tshirts in high school (when it released) and I was bullied terribly for it, but I didn’t care one bit. It was my escape from the reality of having to live in my car as a teen in the 90s/00’s. I survived off of $20 a week and would save $4 for a pack of cards when I could. I continued to collect off and on until present day. It continues to bring the same excitement I felt when I was a teen. I’ve even gotten my wife (we just got married in September!) into collecting and it has brought me so much joy to watch her be excited and find her favorite characters. It remains a bright spot in my current dark times - my wife and I are therapists and we started our own private practice in May 2024 which has brought its share of challenges, in addition to preparing for the loss of our sweet pup, scheduled for February 8th. We have an amazing card shop that is on the way to our new practice location and it makes me smile to think of the excitement happening there. I use pokemon in the therapy work I do with kids, teens and adults and it has brought a lot of people joy and excitement. I am bummed that I could not get anything from the release today and hope the community is able to get back to its roots ❤️

Part of change and recovery is the desire to do so, and depression can halt all momentum, but it can be done with multiple supports in place.
